label: rem:chain-ring-comparison-interpretation
title: Parameter-free derivation chain and the factor of $1/2$
html:
The pairwise Hopf-link estimate of the cyclisation barrier is a factor of two above the threading-link estimate. The two estimates differ only in the linking number they assign to the ring: N for N Hopf links, N/2 for T(2,N).

Derivation chain. The reduced Alexander weights are topological: at q = 1 they are linking numbers and need no input. Two inputs are not derived. The proportionality between crossing energy and reduced Alexander weight is a hypothesis (19.2.7). The molecular energy quantum |q + q^{-1}|_{\mathrm{mol}} \sim 1\text{--}2 eV is a chosen scale, not derived from the substrate parameter q_0, which is pinned by calibration CAL-2.

The factor of 1/2. The ratio of the two estimates is \tilde\Delta_{T(2,6)}(1) / 6 = 3/6 = 1/2, a ratio of linking numbers.

Predictions for other even-N rings. The same framework predicts barriers for even-N cyclic molecules. See Table 3. The barrier increases with N, but the threading efficiency ratio is constant for all even N.

Experimental data. See Table 1. See Table 2.
